transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 72 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Ramos, Hannah Lee, Evan Brooks (Redwood); Sanjay Patel, Lila Morgan, Tom Becker, Priya Nair (BlueRidge)

Summary: quick introductions, walked through proposed ephemeral vault approach, discussed how prompts are ingested/stored, redaction heuristics, workload numbers for POC, timeline and next steps.

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on this account. Diego's our SE who will run the bench and Hannah's the CE who'll help with integration. Evan is on sec and policy. Over to you Sanjay to set the context for the POC.

[00:00:20] Sanjay Patel: Yeah thanks Maya. BlueRidge is building a teletriage assistant for clinicians, so prompts often contain PHI — patient names, dates, small notes. We want to avoid storing prompts long-term, but still need telemetry for debugging and quality. The ask for the POC is basically: can Redwood provide ephemeral prompt storage, deterministic redaction that we can verify, and throughput for typical clinic loads.

[00:00:47] Diego Ramos: Thanks, that's super clear. Two quick clarifying q's — one, when you say ephemeral, are you looking for zero-persist by default, or ephemeral with time-limited encrypted storage for debugging windows?

[00:01:02] Lila Morgan: Ideally ephemeral with a short retention window we control, like 24 hours, with ability to purge on demand. Also we need redaction that flags PHI with high recall — we were thinking 95%+ on our sample set.

[00:01:16] Tom Becker: Also, we may need a legal hold path in some cases, but that's rare. For the POC let's focus on the normal flow.

[00:01:28] Hannah Lee: Noted. We'll show two modes — stateless ephemeral (no disk persist) and short-term encrypted storage using per-tenant envelope encryption with KMS. Evan, we flagged the KMS bit for you earlier — any constraints?

[00:01:42] Evan Brooks: We support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM-backed key stores for Private / Dedicated customers. For hosted POC we can offer BYOK integration with AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault. There are some differences in audit log surface area; we'll document those.

[00:01:58] Priya Nair: HIPAA's auditability is key. We need detailed logs but also need those logs to be redacted for PHI — telemetry should not leak patient identifiers.

[00:02:12] Diego Ramos: Right, so two parallel requirements: (A) user-level logs and tracing for performance and (B) telemetry aggregated and stripped of PII for analytics. In practice we do prefix KV cache caching and continuous batching — we'll ensure the telemetry pipeline has explicit redaction steps and a separate ephemeral audit log option that is time-limited.

[00:02:34] Sanjay Patel: Can you quantify the workload for the POC? What numbers should we expect to test?

[00:02:40] Maya Chen: Sanjay, from our side we'd propose a benchmark scenario representative of 25 concurrent clinician sessions with peak of 5 requests per session per minute and average prompt size of ~350 tokens. That gives us about 4,375 tokens/min peak. For throughput testing we can scale to 100 concurrent sessions to stress batching behavior.

[00:03:06] Tom Becker: That seems reasonable. Latency SLOs? Clinicians need near-interactive responses.

[00:03:12] Diego Ramos: Our target POC success SLO for chat-style assistant: 95th percentile latency <300ms for prompt->first-token when using the optimized hosted model, and end-to-end <700ms for full response on average prompt lengths. If you want a stricter 99th <500ms we can try but it will depend on batching and model choice.

[00:03:33] Lila Morgan: For compliance, redaction accuracy trumps small latency wins. We want to set redaction targets: 95% recall for PHI detection and deterministic redaction with an explainable mapping so we can audit what was redacted.

[00:03:49] Hannah Lee: Agreed. We'll propose a combined approach: heuristic regex rules + model-based entity detection tuned on your annotated samples. Deterministic redaction means we keep a hashed token map (salted HMAC) that allows correlation without storing raw PII. That mapping can be stored in the ephemeral vault and rotated.

[00:04:09] Priya Nair: The mapping approach sounds good, but we need to ensure the salt and keys are customer-controlled. We cannot have raw hashes that are reversible by Redwood.

[00:04:21] Evan Brooks: Customer-controlled keys are supported in our Private stack; for hosted POC we can demo BYOK where the KMS performs envelope encryption and Redwood never sees plaintext keys. We'll annotate the architecture doc with the threat model.

[00:04:37] Sanjay Patel: Benchmarks — what exactly will you run, Diego?

[00:04:42] Diego Ramos: We'll run three baseline tests: 1) throughput baseline with stateless ephemeral path (no storage) to measure pure inference latency; 2) transient storage path with 24h retention, encryption and redaction pipeline to measure overhead; 3) failure/fallback test where the primary model is unavailable and we fall back to a smaller quantized variant and measure quality delta. We'll use your annotated prompt set for redaction accuracy checks.

[00:05:06] Tom Becker: For quality delta we'll need a simple eval rubric — e.g., clinician-validated utility score on 50 sample prompts.

[00:05:13] Maya Chen: Yes, that will be in the SOW. Success criteria proposal now: redaction recall >=95% on annotated sample; 95th pctl latency <300ms stateless path; end-to-end latency <700ms for stored path; throughput: sustain 25 concurrent sessions with headroom for 4x peak during stress run. Also deliverable: post-POC report with logs, benchmarks, and suggested config changes.

[00:05:38] Lila Morgan: One more: telemetry retention options — need to be able to set retention per environment and a purge API to delete all prompts for a given patient id if requested.

[00:05:48] Hannah Lee: We'll provide a purge API in the POC harness, and a demo of on-demand purge as part of the week 3 activities.

[00:05:55] Diego Ramos: Timeline suggestion: Week 0 (this week) — kickoff and infra prep; Week 1 — integrate sample flows and run baseline stateless benchmark; Week 2 — enable ephemeral vault and redaction pipeline and run redaction accuracy tests; Week 3 — scale stress tests, failure/fallback and purge demo; Week 4 — compile results, knowledge transfer and final report.

[00:06:17] Sanjay Patel: That's tight but OK. We'll aim to get sample datasets and engineering point-of-contact assigned.

[00:06:25] Priya Nair: A question on logs: how much detail are you planning to keep in audit logs? We need sequence numbers/timestamps, model id, prompt-hash (not raw), decision flags from redactor and operator id for any manual review.

[00:06:38] Evan Brooks: That's exactly our plan. Audit line items will include event type, model version, redaction decisions, and pointers to ephemeral vault entries (hash ids). We will also ensure logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) with PII redaction applied.

[00:06:55] Tom Becker: Any regulatory concerns around egress if we use Redwood-hosted? Data residency? BlueRidge wants EU/US only — some patients are EU-based.

[00:07:06] Maya Chen: For POC hosted we can run regionally by selecting infra region; for longer-term you can move to Dedicated or Private to pin data regionally. We'll call out region in the SOW.

[00:07:16] Lila Morgan: Also, how will you validate redaction correctness? We will do manual review but prefer an automated metric.

[00:07:23] Diego Ramos: We'll provide a diff-based evaluation: run redactor over annotated data and compute precision/recall/F1 over entity spans. We'll also run synthetic poisoning tests (edge cases like phone numbers without separators) to measure false negatives.

[00:07:39] Sanjay Patel: Sounds good. A couple of operational asks: can we get access to a demo tenant with RBAC where only certain roles can un-redact for debug?

[00:07:48] Hannah Lee: Yes, RBAC scoped to team, and any un-redaction action will be logged with reason and operator id. We'll demo that in week 3.

[00:07:57] Priya Nair: For the SOW please include explicit acceptance criteria and a list of artifacts we'll get at the end (raw benchmark results, sanitized logs, redaction eval report, runbook).

[00:08:09] Maya Chen: Will do. We'll draft the pilot SOW and send by Monday. Quick recap of action items: Maya to send SOW/pricing; Diego to share benchmark runbooks; Evan to send KMS/HSM gap doc; Lila to supply annotated prompts. Agreed?

[00:08:24] Sanjay Patel: Agreed. Thank you.

[00:08:29] Maya Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark windows.

[00:08:36] (Call ends)

Notes about transcription quality: speaker overlap occasionally mis-attributed, some technical terms like "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash" and PII examples anonymized by auto-redaction in the transcript.
